# Local ureq 3.4.2 patch

This directory copies the existing cached crates.io package with the code addition below and removal of one trailing blank line in CONTRIBUTING.md for the repository whitespace check. Original Cargo metadata, licenses and `.cargo_vcs_info.json` are retained; upstream source identity is `2e9ef24a80e1e7ecd0e6604f98ba49aceb7ec322`. The repository's issue #225 Mapbox token adapter needs urllib's raw capped-response behavior while reusing the existing per-socket HTTP transport.

`src/body/mod.rs` adds one method, `Body::as_raw_reader(&mut self) -> impl std::io::Read + '_`. It returns the existing borrowed `BodySourceRef`, retaining HTTP transfer decoding/framing and body-handler completion/drop behavior, while bypassing content decompression and charset conversion. A caller can cap actual bytes with `Read::take`. Existing `as_reader`, consumers, parser, transport and default decoding remain unchanged. No unsafe code or new dependencies are added by this patch.

The focused validation records default-decoded versus raw gzip/Brotli responses, partial-read/drop followed by the next request, and the Mapbox adapter's source comparisons under `.omo/evidence/225-mapbox-tokens/`. Evidence remains local. The workspace patch entry and lock/dependency wiring are owned by the coordinating server worker.

The Xiaoge proxy follow-up preserves the `Content-Encoding` value that the existing response builder removes when transparent decoding is enabled. `RawContentEncoding(pub http::HeaderValue)` is an additive response extension containing that removed value. Callers of the existing raw reader can inspect this extension to apply their own content decoder. Ordinary response headers, `Content-Length` removal, default body readers and transfer framing retain the provider behavior. Only the removed value is moved into the extension; no whole header map is copied and no parser, reader or configuration option is added. The exact Xiaoge failure and corrected source/native scenarios are under `.omo/evidence/225-xiaoge/`; the existing raw-versus-decoded TCP control also verifies metadata and default-reader behavior.

`InitialBodyFullyBuffered(pub bool)` separately reports whether a length-delimited response's complete declared body was already in the unconsumed native transport input buffer when headers completed. It is absent for chunked, close-delimited and bodyless responses. The computation uses checked length conversion and the existing buffer view, with no read, parser or timer. This is native buffer state and does not guarantee identical network feed partitioning with another provider. Xiaoge interprets it only at the independently observed truncated-deflate error/deadline boundary; ordinary readers and response framing remain unchanged.
